olivia (Support): Hey team — ACME reported ~2k objects still returning in search after their configured 30-day TTL. They say the account migrated last week and some objects should've been purged. Can SRE + Security triage?
rajesh (SRE): Got it. Do we have the account id + example object ids? Also asking whether they used the default retention or a custom policy on the old tenant.
acme-prod (Customer): Account ID 987654, sample key obj_78a9 and obj_9f32. We set a custom retention of 30d on the old org, but the new org is on default 90d. We expected 30d to follow objects.
anita (Security): Important: migration should preserve object metadata incl. retention flag. If the custom retention didn't copy, objects might inherit default 90d. Need audit logs for retention policy updates and any retention override events around the migration timestamp.
marta (Legal): Also flag for legal — they need confirmation whether any objects under litigation hold were affected. Please include tombstone/provenance.
rajesh (SRE): Repro steps requested from ACME: how did they migrate? API vs export/import UI? If they used export/import we may have lost preserve-mode headers.
acme-prod (Customer): We used our internal script hitting the export API then the ingest API in the destination. We included metadata in the payload. I can paste the ingest call: ```POST /v1/objects/bulk
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>\nBody: [{"id":"obj_78a9","created_at":1672000000,"retention_ttl":2592000}]```
olivia (Support): Thanks. Rajesh — can you check mutation logs for the ingest timeframe for Account 987654 and see if retention_ttl was accepted or normalized? Also any KMS errors recorded?
rajesh (SRE): Checking now. Quick note: deploy-bot shows a KMS rotate event around 1672000300 which overlapped the ingest window. If the ingest attempted encryption with a key id that was temporarily disabled, we might have queued writes or returned 202 with a delayed commit. Looking at logs: I see several responses 202 Accepted then later errors: `kms:Decrypt failed` and `object_write: queued_for_retry`.
anita (Security): KMS errors during ingest can cause metadata rewrite on retry paths. Need to confirm whether retries reapply original retention metadata or default. Policy says: retry path should preserve client-supplied metadata; but there's a known bug in 1.14.2 where fallback worker re-issued a put without retention header, causing default to be applied.\rajesh (SRE): Confirmed: several queued writes were processed by worker v1.14.2 at 1672000800 and the write path omitted retention header — they defaulted to org default (90d).
acme-prod (Customer): Oh no. So data may have been ingested with wrong TTL. Can you restore original TTL or reapply 30d retroactively? We need to know deletion timeline and whether anything was purged already.\marta (Legal): Need immutable record of what happened and timeline before we consider any data reprocessing.
olivia (Support): Next steps: 1) SRE to produce list of affected object ids + current TTL values. 2) Security to confirm if we can safely update retention_ttl retroactively without violating integrity/compliance. 3) Ops to check if any objects already tombstoned/purged. 4) Inform customer of ETA.
rajesh (SRE): I'll run a scan query: `select id, retention_ttl, created_at from objects where account_id=987654 and created_at between 1671999000 and 1672003000` — returning ~2,078 rows. Dumping to /tmp/acme-987654-ttl.csv and pushing to secure-share.
anita (Security): Policy check: retroactive shortening of retention only allowed if customer-authorized and no legal hold. If we extend shorter TTL to longer retention (i.e., make it 30d < 90d) that's shortening, so need explicit consent and audit entry. If anything is under legal hold, do not modify.
acme-prod (Customer): We authorize reapplying the original 30d TTL to the affected objects. No legal hold on these object IDs. Please proceed but provide an auditable changelog.\rajesh (SRE): Understood. Plan: 1) create a patch job that sets retention_ttl on affected IDs to 2592000. 2) write an audit log entry per object: `retention_update: from 7776000 -> 2592000 via support-patch job #4321 by rajesh`. 3) run job in dry-run on a 10 item sample first.
olivia (Support): Good. Can SRE attach the dry-run logs here and confirm there is no purge race (i.e., object already tombstoned)?
rajesh (SRE): Dry-run done — sample 10 updated in metadata only, no tombstones. Adding logs: `dry-run-update.log` uploaded to secure-share (link redacted). Full job scheduled at 1672010000.\anita (Security): I'll review patch code and confirm audit format before run. Also will request a temporary retention freeze on account to prevent concurrent purge jobs until patch completes.
marta (Legal): Once patch runs, provide the changelog export for legal.
olivia (Support): ETA to customer: patch scheduled in ~2 hours after Security signoff. Customer, we'll update once complete and include the audit export + confirmation that objects are now set to 30d and deletion timeline adjusted.
acme-prod (Customer): Thanks. Please keep us posted and include command outputs.
deploy-bot: KMS rotate event logged at 1672000300 for key `hk-prod-7`. Rotate status: completed.
rajesh (SRE): Post-patch status: job #4321 completed. 2,078 objects updated, audit entries generated. No tombstones found. Will attach final CSV of updates and API call used: `PATCH /v1/objects/batch_retention` with body sample: `[{"id":"obj_78a9","retention_ttl":2592000}]`.
olivia (Support): Closing loop for now. Security/Legal — any objections to marking this as resolved?\anita (Security): No objections. Will keep freeze for 1 hour to ensure no race.
marta (Legal): Accepted. Logging for litigation readiness attached.
acme-prod (Customer): Confirmed — we see TTL updated and deletion timeline now matches expectations. Thanks all :thumbsup:
